items.description:
Brought to New York by a special event, a Black family from Detroit takes in the Guggenheim and Central Park and the look and feel of the architecture and signage of the city in the early 1960s. They film themselves enjoying cafes and restaurants, then attend an award event and banquet where members of the Black community are honored before heading west back to Michigan.

items.title: [Frank Putnam Flint Memorial Fountain Interviews]
items.description:
Content advisory: Racist remarks.

Across several sequences, a television news journalist interviews passersby for their views about whether the Frank Putnam Flint Memorial fountain in Los Angeles should be torn down, primarily  focusing on its maintenance needs, and also with reference to an incident in which a person had drowned in the fountain. Interviewees express a range of remarks, accents, and speech performances, not all of which relate to the fountain and some of which contain racist remarks. The interviewer bypasses potential Black interview subjects.

reel notes: 
"Mag Sound - TV interview Monument"

items.title: Home Movie: 099848
items.description:
In the late 1930s, women with cars and cameras took off to explore the Mojave desert's landscape and native plant communities, following sections of Route 66 and documenting a mountain mining community before turning northwest to the great Central Valley where they documented the noted superbloom of 1938 and the phenomenon of superbloom tourism. Also with visits to the Pacific Ocean, to friends and family members at home in Southern California, and a visit to San Miguel Mission.

Article about superbloom tourism https://www.cnps.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/theguardian.com-The-dazzling-troubling-history-of-California-superbloom-tourism.pdf retrieved 7/2/2026

can notes: 
"Trip 1937-38 / Southern Calif."

items.title: Home Movie: Phal Collection: 011821
items.description:
Content warnings: The file appended _001 contains images of the aftermath of a violent vehicle collision and possibly injured persons. The file appended _002 contains an inclusion of Castle News footage covering an exchange of attacks between Japanese forces and American forces in World War II with racist language and bombing footage.

The black and white sequences of this reel are appended _001, while the color sequences are scanned to a separate file appended _002. 

The black and white reel was created in the 1920s and shows a family in real estate embracing the natural beauty of San Francisco Bay, playing on its hills with the Bay in the background, and celebrating new homes and offices in East Bay cities. The family also engages in subsistence fishing in the Bay with historically significant documentation of fish stocks as they were in the 1920s as well as the East Bay landscape as it appeared with little development.

The color file was created in the 1930s and early 1940s, showing the family at home and at work in the East Bay, as well as fishing in the Bay and boating in the Delta and includes the newsreel sequence mentioned in the content advisory which is in black and white.

items.title: Home Movie: Patrick Marks Collection: 096351
items.description:
In the most unique scene in this reel, a northern California family gathers for the processing of Abalone at a coastal cabin, with an elder in a wetsuit grinning as children look on while expert hands process the haul. This sequence jumps out among others that are centered on landscape photography of the terrain, with studied views of mountains and forests, coastlines and hillscapes, and with a visit to Fort Ross and a ride on the Skunk train.

Note in can: 
"Sept 1963 / Golden Gate to Weaverville / Part I"

items.title: Home Movie: Patrick Marks Collection: 096352
items.description:
Historical ecology of salmon stocks in the Sacramento River ecosystem are documented in this reel that also takes in the lost 19th century town of Whiskeytown, later drowned during the creation of Whiskeytown Lake. With extensive photography of the Trinity Alps area including Shasta Dam and Lake Shasta, with driving perspectives of area roads, time spent at a campsite on the shore of Lake Shasta, and landscape photography of the region's geophysical and cultural features from many perspectives.

Note in can: 
"Trinity Lake & Dam / Sept. 1963 / Part II"

Information on leader states: 
"Weaverville- Trinity Lake- Sept 1963 / Part II" / "Weaverville-Trinity-End / Part II"

items.title: Home Movie: Rick Laubscher Collection: 010417
items.description:
Content advisory: Animal cruelty in the form of bullfights.

The people, architecture, landscape and markets of Mexico in the 1930s are at the heart of this reel, created by tourists from San Francisco who take a road trip through southwestern deserts and travel to Mexico City. With photography of the Sonoran Desert on the way, 1930s clothes and cars, and with a visit to Teotihuacan, its Pyramid of the Moon, and the mountains around the city.

items.title: Cal State Colleges: San Francisco State College
items.description:
Documents scenes within the Third World Liberation Front strikes of 1968 at San Francisco State College (now San Francisco State University). Includes voiceover interviews with students and police officers involved.

More information on the Third World Liberation Front strikes of 1968: https://magazine.sfsu.edu/archive/archive/fall_08/strike.html (accessed 7/7/2025)
